title: Multan rises, 1848
hookLine: a handover at a fortress city, an attack at the gate, and a revolt that leads to a second war

lines: A FORTRESS CITY IN THE SOUTH.
cards: Multan, a walled fortress city in the south of the Punjab. Its governor, Diwan Mulraj, has said he will step down. A new governor rides in to take his place, with British officers from Lahore beside him.
They look over the fort. They receive the keys. Then they turn their horses toward the gate, and a soldier of the garrison steps forward with a spear.
Within days the city is in open revolt, and before long the Punjab is at war again.

teach.b: After the first war, officers of the East India Company sat close to the court at Lahore, with a heavy hand in its decisions.

Mulraj had governed Multan for that court, and he was in a dispute with Lahore over the revenue the province owed. So he offered to resign, and a new governor came down with British officers to take charge.
As the officers left the fort, men of the garrison set on them and wounded them. They took shelter outside the walls, and soon after they were killed there.
Did Mulraj give the order? That has never been fully settled. Some histories say he planned the rising from the start.
Others say his own soldiers struck first and he was swept along, unable or unwilling to turn back once blood was shed.
Herbert Edwardes, a British officer who gathered local fighters and marched on Multan, wrote his own account, and even his story leaves room for doubt.

Then the revolt spread. Other Sikh leaders, angry at a kingdom now run from outside, joined it, Sher Singh Attariwala among them. And the governor-general, Lord Dalhousie, chose not a local settlement but a second war.
In the saloks of Sheikh Farid, kept in the Guru Granth Sahib, Farid tells the reader to answer evil with good, and not to let anger fill the mind. A spear at a gate is a small thing.
At Multan, it set a whole country burning.

how: Sikh histories tell the rising at Multan as the start of the second war with the British, a local quarrel over a handover that grew into a war for the whole Punjab.

o: a revolt at Multan that grew into a second war

games.q: you're Mulraj. men of your garrison have attacked the British officers at your gate. what happens next, as the histories tell it?
o: you hand the attackers over to Lahore.
you stay with the revolt and hold the city.
games.why: Mulraj stayed with the rising and held Multan; whether he chose it or was trapped by it is still argued.

practice: Bring to mind one small thing that has irritated you lately, a tone in a message, a remark at work, a door left open again, and look at it the way you'd watch a lit match, without blowing on it and without throwing it anywhere.
Notice how much heat it really has, breathe out slowly, and let it burn down on its own. If you pray, you can say Waheguru on the out-breath.

wordCard.voice: Multan rises. A handover at a fortress city turns into an attack at the gate, and the attack becomes the revolt that leads to a second war. Today's word.
